_meta.description: Jammu & Kashmir (UT) district & sessions court formatting rules — drives cause-title, party designations, prayer language, verification format
_meta.post_reorganisation_note: Post the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (in force 31 October 2019), the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir was bifurcated into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The Constitution of India applies in full; the Ranbir Penal Code, J&K CrPC and J&K Evidence Act stand repealed and the BNS / BNSS / BSA apply (subject to transitional savings). The common High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh continues to supervise the subordinate judiciary.
_meta.change_protocol: CLO sign-off required for any change. Vishal raises Jira tickets to Ajay for additions; never edits unilaterally.

designation: IN THE COURT OF PRINCIPAL DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, governed by the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 read with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and BNSS, 2023 (extended to the UT post-2019). Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. The UT of J&K presently comprises 20 districts spread across the Kashmir Division (Srinagar HQ) and Jammu Division (Jammu HQ), and the subordinate judiciary is supervised by the common High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh which sits at Srinagar (summer) and Jammu (winter). Urdu remains the official language of the erstwhile State records though pleadings are predominantly in English; Hindi and Urdu are commonly used at district level.

party_designation.state: Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of UT of Jammu and Kashmir, Srinagar/Jammu (as applicable)

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Post Article 370 abrogation (5 August 2019) and the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (in force 31 October 2019), all Central laws apply in full to the UT of J&K. Ranbir Penal Code (RPC), J&K CrPC and J&K Evidence Act stand repealed; BNS, BNSS and BSA apply (subject to savings for pending matters under S.531 BNSS).

Pleadings before the High Court of J&K and Ladakh and the subordinate courts are predominantly in English. Urdu is the official language of record under historical usage; vernacular filings are permitted at district level with English translation.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) before the Sessions Court must disclose any prior rejection by a Magistrate or co-ordinate court.

Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit, certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension. The pre-2019 J&K position that S.438 CrPC did not apply stands superseded.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the J&K High Court Rules, 1999 to be filed at the first instance with requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 (extended to J&K vide the Reorganisation Act); ad valorem fee structure applies to civil suits.

Atrocities (SC/ST), POCSO, NDPS and UAPA cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the UT administration — typically the Principal District & Sessions Judge at the district headquarters.

The High Court of J&K and Ladakh sits at Srinagar (summer capital) from May to October and at Jammu (winter capital) from November to April under the 'Darbar Move' tradition, now partially digitised; subordinate courts follow the seat applicable to their division.

Border districts (Kupwara, Baramulla, Bandipora, Poonch, Rajouri, Kathua, Samba) and frontier sub-divisions follow security-sensitive calendars; record-of-rights and revenue forums under the J&K Land Revenue Act interface frequently with civil jurisdiction.

Srinagar (Kashmir Division HQ) and Jammu (Jammu Division HQ) host the principal district court establishments. The Designation of the senior-most judge in each district is 'Principal District & Sessions Judge', not 'District & Sessions Judge', under the J&K Subordinate Courts (Designation) Rules.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Srinagar, Jammu and a few district headquarters via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory UT-wide. CIS 3.2 is the prevailing case management system.
